prospect.training_background: Played basketball at a high level in France and was athletic through his youth across many sports; last played basketball at least five years ago and found it very difficult even then. Stopped training for years — 'I abandoned myself a little bit for some years'. Recently restarted with a home gym comprising a bench and a pull-up station, training three days a week, and describes the restart as painful and demoralising. Also skates and hikes, both of which provoke knee pain. No kettlebell experience beyond owning a 10-12kg bell.
prospect.medical: Lower back pain daily, which he attributes to prolonged sitting — 'My back is telling me that every day'. Knee pain on both sides of the kneecap, provoked by skating and hiking, which he self-diagnoses as a gait compensation: he walks on his toes rather than the whole foot, so the glute does not engage and the load transfers to the knee. Severe generalised stiffness — he cannot sit cross-legged with his thighs to the floor because of hip tension, though he can touch his toes. Significant excess weight: he reports that last year putting on socks was difficult because of abdominal fat and that he felt he was suffocating, and currently 'my body weighs a ton, and it's like I can't lift my body'. Reports that all current training is painful. No injury or health-conditions question was asked; the rep did ask follow-ups once the prospect raised the back and knees.

notable.note: The clearest ICP mismatch in the batch. The stated ICP explicitly excludes people who are substantially overweight and struggling, and this prospect describes not being able to lift his own body weight, finding every session painful, and having found it hard to put socks on because of abdominal fat — while also having daily lower back pain and knee pain he attributes to a gait compensation. He was taken through a full pitch and a $6,000 ask with no injury or health-conditions question asked at any point and no clinician clearance suggested. Commercially the call has two structural problems. The price landed cold — his audible 'Whoa... I wasn't expecting that' means P1 never framed a decision — and the primary payment route offered was Payva, a US financing provider, to a buyer in France whose availability the rep could not confirm and did not check. The rep did do one thing better than anywhere else in this batch: he asked outright what cash was actually available and got a real number, $2,000.

quality.notes: Attribution is inverted throughout and degrades badly in the closing twenty minutes. From roughly 01:39:35 the two speakers are repeatedly merged inside single blocks, and one passage duplicates the rep's payment-structure explanation verbatim across two consecutive turns attributed to different speakers, which is a processing artefact rather than genuine repetition. The financing provider name is mangled several times in transcription ('Paiva', 'Payva', 'Pava', 'P-A-Y-V-V-V-A'), and the prospect is a non-native English speaker which compounds the segmentation errors. Roles were read from content throughout. No height or weight exists in this record because none was asked. This is the second of two consecutive and unrelated sales calls in one Drive file, running from 01:02:56 to the end.
